title: Can You Remove a Rake Before Playing?
question: Your ball comes to rest next to a bunker. A rake is lying on the ground beside your ball and is in the way of your swing. Can you move the rake before playing your shot?

choices.text: No. Once your ball has come to rest, nothing nearby may be moved.
Yes. A rake is a movable obstruction and may be moved without penalty.
Yes, but only if your ball does not move.
No. You must either play around the rake or take unplayable ball relief.

explanation: A bunker rake is a movable obstruction. You may move it at any time without penalty. If moving the rake causes your ball to move, you must replace the ball on its original spot, and there is no penalty for causing it to move while removing a movable obstruction. Many golfers think they have to leave the rake where it is once the ball has come to rest, but that is incorrect. (Rule 15.2a, Rule 15.2a(1))
